steps: Inspect & prepare the fireplace

Verify a clean, non-combustible masonry or factory-built solid-fuel fireplace and chimney that meet the opening minimums. Block the flue damper fully open or remove it, and remove the existing chimney cap.

• Clean the chimney and fireplace to keep creosote odor out of the home; verify combustible mantel and sidewall clearances (Section 8.0).
  • Refractory, glass doors, screen rails, screen mesh and log grates may be removed. Removed parts must be capable of re-installation if the insert is ever removed (removing rivets or screws is acceptable).
  • Factory-built fireplace with no gas access hole: drill one of 1½" (37.5mm) or less through the lower sides or bottom of the firebox, and plug it with non-combustible insulation once the gas line is in.
  • Provide electrical power; the outlet box location is in Figure 2.1 (p. 9).
  • Mechanically attach the 'THIS UNIT HAS BEEN MODIFIED' label and the gas-insert-only conversion warning at the bottom of the existing firebox, where they will be visible if the insert is removed.
Cut the liner & fit the cap

Measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney, subtract the insert height, and cut the #816 3" flexible pipe to that length. Slide the intake pipe (end without a collar) over cap collar A and the sealed, red-marked exhaust pipe onto collar B, each fixed with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided).

The exhaust and combustion-air pipes must go to their correct collars on both the termination cap and the insert's vent adapter. The insert's exhaust collar is on the right, so install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right.

  1. Measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney (easier with two people) and subtract the insert height: that is the length of co-linear flexible pipe needed. Cut the #816 (36' [10.97m] of 3" flexible pipe) to it.
  2. Carefully extend both pipes to the total length.
  3. Slide the combustion-air intake pipe (end without a collar) over collar A and secure with (3) self-tapping screws.
  4. Bead sealant around the inner edge of the exhaust pipe end (red marking), slide it onto collar B, secure with (3) self-tapping screws and seal around the joint.

Avoid tight bends that could abrade or damage the flexible pipes.
Run the vent system

Slide the vent adapter back out of its channels on top of the insert. Feed both 3" x 3" flexible pipes down the chimney, seal and set the termination cap per the vent maker's instructions, and pull both pipes into the firebox.

• Offsets in the chimney: guide each pipe end with its own weighted rope. Never tie one rope around both pipes.
  • To prevent cold-air drafts and heat loss, Hussong recommends insulating with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136: optionally around the first 3' (914mm) below the cap (secured with wire) and between the pipes and the chimney.
  • Set the cap on a liberal bead of sealant around the top of the chimney. The #816-CAP can also be fixed with 2" (50mm) self-tapping screws and anchor straps (not provided) through its side pilot holes.
Connect to the vent adapter

Set the vent adapter in the fireplace opening. Seal the red-marked exhaust pipe inside the collar marked 'Exhaust' and the intake pipe over the intake collar, each secured with (3) ½ in (13mm) self-tapping screws and extra sealant at the joint.
Place, seat & level the insert

Slide the insert in until the channels on top line up with the vent adapter, draw the adapter forward with the pull rod until seated, and fix it with (2) ½ in (13mm) sheet metal screws. Level with the leveling bolts (2 each side) if needed.

1. Slide the insert into the opening until the channels on top of the appliance align with the vent adapter.
  2. Put the pull rod handle through the access slot at the top and hook it through the hole in the pull rod. Push the insert in while pulling the adapter forward until seated.
  3. Secure the adapter through the slots at the top with (2) ½ in (13mm) sheet metal screws (components packet).
  4. Use the pull rod handle to pull the vent adapter back to starting position, remove the pull handle and verify the vent connection.
  5. If needed, thread the leveling bolts (components packet) into the nuts at the bottom of the insert, 2 each side.

Into a minimum-size opening, the gas line may have to be run after placement.
Gas line connection

Connect a listed ½" tee-handle manual shut-off valve and flexible connector to the ½" control valve inlet, running the line preferably through the right gas line hole and clear of the fan. Check all connections for leaks with soapy water.

• Qualified person only, per local codes (otherwise ANSI Z223.1); in Massachusetts, a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Supplied: a 3/8" (10mm) x 18" (457mm) flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve.
  • Supply-piping pressure tests: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Manufactured for natural gas. For propane, follow the conversion kit instructions, and convert before installing the log set.
  • High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or the authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
Shroud, louver & grille

Remove the glass and fasten the shroud to the mounting nuts on the insert's sides with (4) truss head screws, without sealing the existing fireplace's ventilation or draft-relief openings. Fit the upper louver on the short screws and the lower grille on the long screws.

• Upper louver: start the short screws halfway into the holes along the shroud's upper edge, slide the louver's slots over them at the depth you want, then tighten.
  • Lower grille: long screws into the mounting nuts in the shroud.
  • CK34-LMK low mantel kit (only with CK34-PSF or CK34-RSF barriers): slide the heat deflector under the screen front's mounting tabs and refit the (2) screws through tab and deflector; the gasket must contact the shroud.
  • The bottom of the fireplace must be level with the finished hearth for the safety barriers to fit, so allow for the hearth finish when building a platform.
Log set, glass & barrier

Finish any propane conversion first, then place the CXL2-500 logs on their pins and notches (numbers are under each log), keeping them off the burner ports. Refit the glass and hang the safety barrier in the shroud's (4) slots.

1. Ember panel 2CX in front of the burner.
  2. Log 1CX: its (2) holes onto the mounting pins at the back of the burner; push down to seat.
  3. Logs 3CX and 4CX: holes onto the mounting pins on the burner.
  4. Logs 5CX and 6CX: into the notches on 1CX and 3CX.
  5. Log 7CX: into the notches in 1CX, 4CX and ember panel 2CX.
  6. Log 8CX: into the notches in 1CX and 4CX.
  7. Spread the rock wool embers over the logs and burner with a stiff bristle brush.

Glass: slots at the top over the firebox tabs, lower it into place, pull the (2) spring-loaded latches out and up. Barrier: tabs on its back into the shroud slots (2 each side), raise slightly and let the tabs lower into position. Never operate with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
Electrical & controls

Plug the three-prong grounding plug into a properly grounded receptacle on a 120VAC supply that is hot at all times (no switch). For a wall switch or thermostat, run low-voltage wires to the TH and TP-TH terminals on the gas valve.

• Never connect 115V to the gas valve; the millivolt gas valve does not require a 110-120 VAC supply.
  • Rocker switch left wired: it must be OFF for the optional controls to work. If it is ON, the burner runs until the rocker is turned OFF; the wall switch or thermostat won't shut it off. Disconnecting its wires from the back of the valve disables it.
  • Mount the wall control or thermostat on a wall near the fireplace and follow its own instructions.
  • Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the appliance and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
Pressure test & flame check

With a manometer on the valve's IN (A) and OUT (B) taps, confirm inlet and manifold pressures against Table 12.1, then re-tighten each tap and verify it reads no pressure. Burn the fireplace and check the flames turn lazy and yellow.

Inlet, tap ANG 5" - 10.5" WC · LP 11" - 13" WC
Manifold, tap BNG 1.6" - 3.5" WC · LP 6.4" - 10" WC

Use a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose. Inlet: test with all other gas appliances on or at full capacity; pilot lit and knob ON (burner should not light), then rocker ON and check the reading is near maximum inlet pressure. Manifold: pilot lit, knob ON, rocker ON. Re-tighten taps snug, not over-tight.

Flames appear blue when first lit and gradually turn yellow during the first 15 minutes. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips, the air shutter may need adjusting by a qualified service technician (see the air shutter card).

panels.title: No spark or pilot won't light
items: No spark at the pilot → check piezo igniter grounding (tighten the mounting fastener) and its wiring to the electrode
Electrode out of position → set a 1/8" (3mm) gap to the pilot; metal contact can arc below the electrode
Sparks but no pilot → no gas: check for multiple shut-off valves in the supply line, or an empty propane tank

panels.title: Pilot won't stay lit
items: Pilot flame not on the thermocouple → clean the pilot hood, adjust the pilot flame at the gas valve
Loose thermocouple → fully inserted, hand tight plus 1/4 turn
Thermocouple below 15 millivolts → replace the thermocouple
Thermopile below 350 millivolts at TH-TP and TP (valve at PILOT) → replace the thermopile
Frequent outages → pilot shield missing, or pilot flame too high or too low

panels.title: Burner won't light or stay lit
items: Knob not at ON, rocker not ON, or no heat demand from the wall switch, remote or thermostat
Faulty switching device → jumper the switch terminals, then the valve terminals, to find a bad switch or bad wiring
Thermopile wires loose at the valve, or pinched and grounding out
Refractory panels (if installed) not tight against the firebox walls
Pilot and burner go out → empty propane tank, glass frame installed wrong, weak thermopile or thermocouple, inner vent pipe leaking exhaust into the firebox, blocked vent cap

panels.title: Glass sooting or lifting flames
items: Glass sooting → log placement, venturi setting (open slightly), vent cap installation or blockage
Blue flame lifting off the burner → venturi setting (p. 37 says open slightly; p. 35 says opening causes it), vent cap installation, vent leak or blockage

light.title: Lighting the pilot
light.html:
You light the pilot by hand, using the gas control knob and the piezo igniter button. To reach the gas valve, lift off the safety screen and open the lower grille.

  1. Read the safety information. Set the thermostat to its lowest setting (if you have one) and turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  2. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.
  3. Wait 5 minutes for any gas to clear. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  4. Find the pilot: follow the metal tube from the gas control into the firebox.
  5. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counterclockwise to PILOT.
  6. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Press the piezo igniter button repeatedly until the pilot lights.
  7. Keep holding the knob in for 1 minute, then let go. It pops back up and the pilot should stay lit. If it goes out, repeat from step 2.
  8. Turn the knob counterclockwise to ON. Turn the power back on and set the thermostat (if you have one).

The ON/OFF rocker switch (or a wall switch, remote or thermostat, if you have one) then runs the main burner.

If the knob doesn't pop back up, stop and call your service technician or gas supplier immediately. If the pilot won't stay lit after several tries, turn the knob to OFF and call your service technician or gas supplier. Use only your hand to push in or turn the knob, and never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it: call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

switch.title: Turning the flame on and off
switch.html:
Once the pilot is lit and the gas control knob is at ON, the main burner is switched on and off separately.

  • ON/OFF rocker switch: ON runs the main burner; OFF turns it off.
  • Wall switch, thermostat or remote (if you have one): these work properly only while the rocker switch is OFF. If the rocker is ON, the burner keeps running until you turn the rocker OFF, and the wall switch or thermostat can't turn it off. Your installer may have disconnected the rocker switch instead.

The gas valve is a millivolt valve: it doesn't need household electricity (110-120 VAC) to operate.

Turn the gas off completely

  1. Set the thermostat to its lowest setting (if you have one).
  2. If the fireplace is going to be serviced, turn off all electric power to it.
  3. Lift off the safety screen and open the lower grille to reach the gas controls.
  4. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF.

flame.title: Adjusting flame height and heat
flame.html:
Your fireplace has a manual HI/LO knob on the gas valve. It sets the main burner's flame height and how much heat the fireplace gives off.

  1. Lift off the safety screen and open the lower grille to reach the gas valve.
  2. Turn the HI/LO knob clockwise toward HI, or counterclockwise toward LO.
  3. Stop when the flame looks and feels the way you want.
  4. Set the grille back in position and put the safety screen back on.
Screen back on, every time. Don't run the fireplace without the safety screen. It's the barrier that helps protect children and others from the hot glass.

If the flames themselves look wrong (dark orange with black tips, or lifting off the burner), that isn't a HI/LO setting. See how the flame should look.

sounds.title: Fog, a paint smell and noises
sounds.html:
Fog on the glass

When you first light the fireplace, condensation appears on the glass. This is normal in all gas fireplaces and disappears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during this time; it helps the paint cure faster.

Noises as it heats and cools

The metal expands as it heats and contracts as it cools, so you may hear some noise. This is normal and doesn't affect how well or how long the fireplace works. The warranty also treats discoloration and this kind of noise as normal, not a defect.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches and don't use a phone in the building. Leave, and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is a homeowner job, once a year. Do it only when the fireplace is completely cool: never clean the glass or take it off while it's hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down, then lift the glass up and off the 2 tabs at the top.
  4. Clean it with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. Hook the slots at the top of the glass over the tabs, lower the bottom into place, and pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  6. Put the safety screen back. Don't run the fireplace without it.
Handle with care. Don't strike or slam the glass. Never run the fireplace with the glass off, cracked or broken. Replacement glass (#700-006T) comes only from Hussong Mfg. as a complete assembly and should be fitted by a qualified service person.

look.title: How the flame should look
look.html:
When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. During the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow. What you want is lazy, yellow flames: those need no adjustment.

Call a qualified service technician if you see

  • Flames that stay blue.
  • Dark orange flames with black tips, or soot building up on the glass.
  • Flames that lift off the burner ("ghosting") or float instead of burning steady.

The burner's air shutter (venturi) is set at the factory, and adjusting it must be done by a qualified service technician. Slight changes have dramatic results. Altitude, fuel quality and the venting also affect how the flame looks.

Logs matter too. Logs placed over the burner ports affect the flame and can cause excessive soot on the glass.

timeout.title: The 7-day pilot time-out
timeout.html:
Some regions require a 7-day time-out. Ask your dealer whether it applies to your installation. If it does, your fireplace has a millivolt Pilot-on-Demand gas valve with a 7-day timer.

  • The timer starts when you light the pilot.
  • Each time the main burner lights during those 7 days, the timer resets to 7 days.
  • If the fireplace isn't used for 7 days in a row, the main burner and/or the pilot turn off. The gas control knob stays where it was (PILOT or ON).

This is a standard safety feature, not a fault. To get it going again you must cycle the system by hand: lift off the safety screen, open the lower grille to reach the gas valve and knob, and relight it using the lighting steps.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building immediately.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass causes burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • The safety barrier in front of the glass protects children and other at-risk people. Keep it on, and replace a damaged one with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely in the same room. A safety gate can keep toddlers away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected by a professional service person before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpets, bedding and the like can mean it needs cleaning more often. Installation and repair are jobs for a qualified service person.

  • Every 6 months, fan: disconnected from power and vacuumed. The bearings are sealed and need no oil.
  • Yearly, firebox: debris vacuumed out; the bottom glass latches checked for spring tension and free movement.
  • Yearly, vent system: examined, so combustion and ventilation air can flow freely.
  • Yearly, glass: cleaned and checked for cracks, scratches and nicks.
  • Yearly, burner and pilot: vacuumed, gas connections leak-checked, pilot flame and millivolt output checked, and the burner confirmed to light within 4 seconds with steady flames.
Your part: keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that burns, and clean the glass once a year.

warranty.title: Limited lifetime warranty
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants this Kozy Heat appliance to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship. Nothing needs to be mailed in to register. Keep your proof of purchase showing the date, with the fireplace's model and serial number.

30 days, parts and laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1, parts and laborAll parts and material except the 30-day items and exclusions
Years 2 to lifetime, parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shield(s), front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids it or isn't covered

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual.
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or the appliance altered or tampered with.
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation.
  • Normal wear and tear, venting or environmental problems, and non-Hussong chimney parts or accessories.

The warranty is nontransferable.

specInput.title: Input rates
specInput.html:
NG max / min36,000 / 22,000 Btu/h (10.55 / 6.49 kW)
LP max / min36,500 / 24,000 Btu/h (10.7 / 7.03 kW)

Manufactured for natural gas; to convert to propane, follow the instructions included with the conversion kit (parts list: Conversion Kit - Propane OCK-S50A, Conversion Kit - NG OCK-S35A). Not convertible to other gases unless a certified kit is used.

Altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level. Canada: above 4,500' (1,372m), reduce the certified high altitude rating 4% for each additional 1,000' (305m).

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5" - 10.5" WC (1.25 - 2.62 kPa)
Propane11" - 13" WC (2.74 - 3.24 kPa)

Test at the IN tap (A) with a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose, with all other gas appliances on or at full capacity. Pilot lit, knob ON (burner should not light): note the reading. Rocker ON: check it is near maximum inlet pressure. Then rocker OFF, knob OFF, tighten the tap snug, relight and confirm the tap reads no pressure.

If inlet pressure is too high or too low, contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust it. Low pressure can cause a delayed ignition.

Disconnect the appliance and its valve during supply-piping tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa).

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas, high / low3.5" / 1.6" WC
Propane, high / low10" / 6.4" WC

Test at the OUT tap (B) with a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose: light the pilot, knob to ON, rocker to ON and note the reading. Tighten the tap snug (don't over tighten) and confirm it is sealed: the manometer should read no pressure with the rocker ON.

Table 12.1 gives the same range: NG 1.6" - 3.5" WC, LP 6.4" - 10" WC.

specBurner.title: Air shutter (venturi)
specBurner.html:
Natural gas, factory set1/16" (2mm) open
Propane, factory set1/2" (13mm) open

Venturi adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician. Let the fireplace cool first, adjust in slight increments, and always burn it at least 15 minutes, then let it cool before any further adjustment. If the glass soots, check log positioning first: logs must not block burner ports.

Dark orange, black tipsVenturi closed too far: open slightly
Short, blue flamesVenturi open too far: close slightly
Lifting (ghosting) flamesGas pressure too high: check manometer; or venturi closed too far: open slightly
Lazy, yellow flamesNo adjustment necessary

To adjust: remove the safety barrier, glass frame assembly, log set and burner; loosen the venturi screw, adjust, re-tighten; reinstall the burner with the venturi over the burner orifice.

Note: p. 35 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner (and Table 12.3 says to close it slightly for short, blue flames), but the troubleshooting chart on p. 37 says a flame that burns blue and lifts off the burner may need the venturi opened slightly.

review.notes: Ignition: millivolt SIT valve with a pilot lit by hand (gas control knob + piezo igniter, p. 32); the main burner runs from the ON/OFF rocker switch or an optional low-voltage wall switch/thermostat/remote (pp. 30, 37). Regions requiring a 7-day time-out get a millivolt Pilot-on-Demand valve (p. 33; parts 700-086N-7 / 700-087A-7). The manual has no remote-control instructions and doesn't say how the fan is switched or whether it is standard (parts list has Fan Kit CSK-028), so the catalog's 'Fan kit included' / blower 'standard' are unverified. Appliance dimensions appear only in Figure 2.1 (p. 9) with garbled fractions and unassigned labels, so catalog height/width/depth were not checked; efficiency, viewing area and ceramic glass are not in the manual. Metric rounding differences not flagged: manifold kPa 0.40 (p. 8) vs 0.41 (p. 34) NG low and 2.49 vs 2.48 LP high (the guide gives manifold in in. WC only); max horizontal run 24" (609mm) on pp. 15-16 vs (610mm) on p. 16; Table 4.1 lists 7.5 ft as 2.27 m (the guide uses feet). Sealant is '(not provided)' in the #816-CAP figure legend (p. 15) but '(provided)' in the p. 17-18 steps; the guide doesn't say either way. Safety barrier part number CK34A-FPDSF2 (p. 11) vs CK34-AFPDSF2 (p. 40); not used in the guide. The p. 32 gas-smell block omits 'Leave the building immediately'; the guide uses the p. 1 version. Step 4 of 6.7 (p. 18) says to use the pull rod handle to pull the vent adapter back to starting position after securing it; transcribed as printed. Massachusetts CO-detector/signage rules (p. 7) are written for sidewall horizontally vented equipment and are left out. Pages 2, 4, 6 and 42 are blank. No French-only or scrambled text needed decoding.
